tasks.short: Pray with members, lead prayer groups, keep the confidential list of prayer requests and write the weekly intentions.

steps.what: Minister prays with members during visits and services
Minister leads prayer groups to promote spirituality
Members send prayer requests through the website form; handed to the minister after services today
Minister keeps a list of prayer requests from members
Minister writes the weekly prayer intentions

tasks.design: Members send prayer requests through a short form on the congregation's website ({CMS}) into a confidential list only the minister sees, with a field for whether the request may be named in services. Praying, leading groups and writing intentions stay with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came on slips of paper and by phone and were copied into a notebook.
tasks.enabler_now: Website forms can feed a confidential list.
tasks.still_hard: Prayer requests are deeply personal; most still come in conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Praying with a family at a deathbed.

reach.learn: Whether a shared confidential list improves follow-up.

evidence.claim: Website forms can feed a confidential list with access for named people only.
Church membership reveals religious belief; a religious body may process it for members but may not disclose it outside without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from members' needs to prayer intentions; pastoral care plans are outside.
Input contract: requests sent by members through the form; fallback is paper slips.
Praying, groups and intentions do not change. Members' time for the form is shown in s5 and is not counted again as new work. s3 keeps 50 for tidying the list and requests still handed over on paper.

incremental.description: Minister reads the confidential list weekly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most members keep handing over paper slips, so s3 keeps 80 (1.6); high: requests through the form as designed (4.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study texts and commentaries, write the sermon, practise and deliver it, and pass the text on for the website.

steps.what: Minister studies the texts, commentaries and earlier sermons to prepare
Minister writes the sermon
Minister practises and delivers sermons in the service
Minister e-mails the sermon text to the website editor

tasks.design: A full-text search over the minister's own sermon archive and the commentaries the congregation has licensed ({DOCS}) shortens looking things up. The sermon text is shared with the website editor from the same document space with one click. Studying, writing and preaching stay with the minister; no AI writes sermons.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier sermons and notes sat in folders and files without search.
tasks.enabler_now: Document spaces offer full-text search across archives and licensed texts.
tasks.still_hard: A sermon speaks to this congregation this week; search only finds material.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the words a grieving congregation needs on Sunday.

reach.learn: Whether a searchable archive helps talk preparation.

evidence.claim: Document spaces offer full-text search across personal archives and licensed texts.

assumptions: Boundary: from chosen readings to the text with the editor; publishing is outside.
Input contract: readings chosen by the minister; licensed commentaries bought by the congregation; fallback is paper folders.
Writing and preaching do not change.
Editor time is outside the minister's savings.

incremental.description: Minister files sermons in the archive.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sermons are filed in the archive and few commentaries are licensed, so s1 keeps 90 (7.5); high: archive and commentaries searchable as designed (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the readings, prepare them in several translations, read them in services and prepare reading sheets for lectors.

steps.what: Minister chooses the readings for services
Minister reads the texts in several translations to prepare
Minister reads from sacred texts in services
Minister prints reading sheets for lectors from the digital edition; copied by hand today

tasks.design: A digital reading schedule ({OTHER}) shows the set readings for each date in the church year, and the licensed digital edition of the sacred text prints reading sheets for lectors from the chosen passages. Preparing and reading in services stay with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were looked up in printed schedules and copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reading schedules and licensed digital editions are available to congregations.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing readings outside the schedule is the minister's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a familiar text so it sounds new.

reach.learn: Whether printed sheets help lectors prepare.

evidence.claim: Reading schedules and digital editions of sacred texts give set readings per date and printable passages.
Modern translations are copyrighted; printing passages needs the publisher's licence for church use.

assumptions: Boundary: from the church calendar to texts read; preaching is outside.
Input contract: reading schedule from the denomination; licensed digital edition bought by the congregation; fallback is printed books.
Preparing and reading do not change. s4 keeps 10 for choosing and printing the sheets.
Lectors' time is outside the minister's savings.
research_questions: Do lectors prepare better with sheets?

incremental.description: No new work: the reading schedule comes from the denomination.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many services use local readings outside the schedule, so s1 keeps 80 (13.0); high: set readings used as designed (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the order of service, ask volunteers to take roles, remind them, write the order of service, send it to the screen team and lead the service.

steps.what: Minister plans the order of service with musicians
Volunteers sign up for roles on the rota page; reply by e-mail today
Minister asks readers and volunteers to take roles in the service
Minister checks the final rota: names, roles, date and service
Minister confirms the checked rota, and the tool reminds volunteers the day before; phoned by the minister today
Minister writes the order of service for the bulletin and screen
Minister checks the final order of service: songs, readings, names and times
Minister sends the checked order of service to the screen team and printer
Minister leads the regular religious service

tasks.design: A shared service planning page ({OTHER}) holds the order of service, songs and readings, and volunteers sign up for roles on a rota there. Once the minister has confirmed the rota, the tool reminds volunteers the day before. A template fills the order of service from the plan for the bulletin and screen; after the minister checks it, it goes to the screen team and printer. Leading the service stays with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans, rotas and orders of service went back and forth by e-mail and phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Service planning tools combine plans, rotas, reminders and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Volunteers drop out late; someone still has to find a replacement.
tasks.human_edge: Leading worship so people feel they belong.

evidence.claim: Service planning tools combine orders of service, volunteer rotas, reminders and templates.
Volunteer and member data reveal religious belief; an external service needs a processor contract.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning to the service held; pastoral follow-up is outside.
Input contract: church calendar from the denomination; volunteers sign up themselves; fallback is e-mail and phone.
Leading the service does not change.
Volunteers' time is shown in s7 as customer time and is not counted again as new work. s3 and s5 keep 20 for the release itself.
research_questions: Do late drop-outs fall with reminders?

already_counted.description: Minister checks the filled order of service.

incremental.description: Minister finds replacements for late drop-outs.

approvals.approved_version: The rota with names, roles and date exactly as checked by the minister in s2b, sent once as reminders to those volunteers the day before; changed roles need a new check.
The order of service exactly as checked by the minister in s4b, sent once to the screen team and the printer; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many volunteers do not use the rota page, so the minister keeps asking and s2 keeps 80 (22.0); high: sign-up as designed (25.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The minister keeps prayer, preaching, reading and leading worship; lists, look-ups and e-mail rounds shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A minister who spends saved hours visiting members.
